theory.intro: These problems give a triangle that is **not** right-angled and ask you to pick the right tool. Match what you are given to the rule: **two sides and the included angle**, or **all three sides**, call for the **cosine rule**; a **complete opposite pair** (a side and the angle facing it) calls for the **sine rule**; **two sides and the included angle** when an **area** is wanted call for the **area rule**. Harder problems are **multistep** — one rule produces a value that a second rule then uses — and **bearings** problems become ordinary triangles once you mark the north lines and find the included angle.
facts: **Two sides and the included angle, find the third side** $\Rightarrow$ cosine rule $c^{2}=a^{2}+b^{2}-2ab\cos C$.
**All three sides, find an angle** $\Rightarrow$ cosine rule rearranged $\cos C=\dfrac{a^{2}+b^{2}-c^{2}}{2ab}$, with the side opposite the wanted angle as $c$.
**A complete opposite pair (a side and its opposite angle)** $\Rightarrow$ sine rule: $\dfrac{a}{\sin A}=\dfrac{b}{\sin B}$ for a side, $\dfrac{\sin A}{a}=\dfrac{\sin B}{b}$ for an angle.
**Two sides and the included angle, find the area** $\Rightarrow$ area rule $A=\dfrac{1}{2}ab\sin C$.
**Multistep:** find an intermediate value with one rule, then feed it into a second. Keep the full calculator value until the final line, then round.

**Bearings** are measured clockwise from north as three figures ($072^{\circ}\text{T}$). A back bearing (the reverse direction) differs by $180^{\circ}$; a north line drawn at a vertex turns two bearings into the included angle of a triangle.
steps: Select the rule that fits what is given
Apply the rule to find the first unknown
Apply a second rule to reach the required value
Convert an angle to a true bearing

foundation.solution_text:
Two sides ($14$ cm and $9$ cm) and the angle **between** them ($62^{\circ}$) are known, and $x$ is the third side.
Two sides and the included angle mean the **cosine rule**: $x^{2}=14^{2}+9^{2}-2(14)(9)\cos 62^{\circ}$.

The $47^{\circ}$ angle and its opposite side ($10$ cm) form a **complete opposite pair**, and $x$ is opposite the known $68^{\circ}$ angle.
A complete opposite pair means the **sine rule**: $\dfrac{x}{\sin 68^{\circ}}=\dfrac{10}{\sin 47^{\circ}}$.

Two sides and the included angle are given, so use the **cosine rule**.
$x^{2}=11^{2}+8^{2}-2(11)(8)\cos 47^{\circ}$
$x=\sqrt{185-176\cos 47^{\circ}}$
$=8.0603\ldots$
$\approx 8.1$ cm

A side ($12$ cm) and its opposite angle ($80^{\circ}$) are a complete pair, so use the **sine rule** with the unknown side on top.
$\dfrac{x}{\sin 35^{\circ}}=\dfrac{12}{\sin 80^{\circ}}$
$x=\dfrac{12\sin 35^{\circ}}{\sin 80^{\circ}}$
$=6.989\ldots$
$\approx 7.0$ cm

All three sides are known, so use the **cosine rule** rearranged for an angle, with the side opposite $\theta$ (the $11$) as $c$.
$\cos\theta=\dfrac{7^{2}+9^{2}-11^{2}}{2(7)(9)}$
$\cos\theta=\dfrac{9}{126}$
$\theta=\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{9}{126}\right)$
$=85.9041\ldots^{\circ}$
$\approx 85.9^{\circ}$

A side ($9$) and its opposite angle ($50^{\circ}$) are a complete pair, so use the **sine rule** with $\sin$ on top; $\theta$ is opposite the $7$.
$\dfrac{\sin\theta}{7}=\dfrac{\sin 50^{\circ}}{9}$
$\sin\theta=\dfrac{7\sin 50^{\circ}}{9}$
$\theta=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{7\sin 50^{\circ}}{9}\right)$
$=36.5706\ldots^{\circ}$
$\approx 36.6^{\circ}$

Two sides and the included angle are given, so use the **area rule**.
$A=\dfrac{1}{2}ab\sin C$
$=\dfrac{1}{2}(13)(10)\sin 68^{\circ}$
$\approx 60.3\text{ cm}^{2}$

Two sides and the included (obtuse) angle are given, so use the **cosine rule**; $\cos 118^{\circ}$ is negative, which lengthens $x$.
$x^{2}=9^{2}+6^{2}-2(9)(6)\cos 118^{\circ}$
$x=\sqrt{117-108\cos 118^{\circ}}$
$=12.95\ldots$
$\approx 13.0$ m

development.solution_text:
1. **Select the rule that fits what is given**
Two sides and the included angle give $AC$ by the **cosine rule**.
$AC^{2}=17^{2}+12^{2}-2(17)(12)\cos 54^{\circ}$
$AC=\sqrt{433-408\cos 54^{\circ}}$
$=13.899\ldots$
$\approx 13.9$ cm
2. **Apply a second rule to reach the required value**
A complete pair ($AC$ opposite $54^{\circ}$) is now known, so use the **sine rule** for $\angle A$, opposite $BC=12$.
$\dfrac{\sin A}{12}=\dfrac{\sin 54^{\circ}}{13.899\ldots}$
$\sin A=\dfrac{12\sin 54^{\circ}}{13.899\ldots}$
$A=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{12\sin 54^{\circ}}{13.899\ldots}\right)$
$\approx 44^{\circ}$

1. **Select the rule that fits what is given**
The area rule needs an angle, but none is given. With three sides, find the angle $C$ between the $8$ m and $11$ m sides (opposite the $15$ m side) by the **cosine rule**.
$\cos C=\dfrac{8^{2}+11^{2}-15^{2}}{2(8)(11)}$
$\cos C=\dfrac{-40}{176}$
$C=\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{-40}{176}\right)=103.136\ldots^{\circ}$
2. **Apply a second rule to reach the required value**
$A=\dfrac{1}{2}(8)(11)\sin 103.136\ldots^{\circ}$
$\approx 42.8\text{ m}^{2}$

1. **Select the rule that fits what is given**
The area rule needs two sides and their included angle; only one side is known. First find the third angle, then a second side. $\angle C=180^{\circ}-55^{\circ}-65^{\circ}=60^{\circ}$, and $AC$ (opposite $\angle B$) comes from the **sine rule**.
$\dfrac{AC}{\sin 65^{\circ}}=\dfrac{60}{\sin 60^{\circ}}$
$AC=\dfrac{60\sin 65^{\circ}}{\sin 60^{\circ}}=62.79\ldots\text{ m}$
2. **Apply a second rule to reach the required value**
Sides $AB=60$ and $AC=62.79\ldots$ meet at $\angle A=55^{\circ}$.
$A=\dfrac{1}{2}(60)(62.79\ldots)\sin 55^{\circ}$
$\approx 1543\text{ m}^{2}$

mastery.solution_text:
1. **Select the rule that fits what is given**
The back bearing of $A$ from $B$ is $048^{\circ}+180^{\circ}=228^{\circ}$, and $C$ is on $128^{\circ}$:
$\angle ABC=228^{\circ}-128^{\circ}=100^{\circ}$.
2. **Apply the rule to find the first unknown**
$AC^{2}=60^{2}+95^{2}-2(60)(95)\cos 100^{\circ}$
$AC=\sqrt{12625-11400\cos 100^{\circ}}$
$=120.849\ldots$
$\approx 121$ km
3. **Apply a second rule to reach the required value**
The **sine rule** gives $\angle ACB$, opposite $AB=60$.
$\dfrac{\sin\angle ACB}{60}=\dfrac{\sin 100^{\circ}}{120.849\ldots}$
$\angle ACB=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{60\sin 100^{\circ}}{120.849\ldots}\right)=29.27\ldots^{\circ}$
4. **Convert an angle to a true bearing**
The bearing of $B$ from $C$ is $128^{\circ}+180^{\circ}=308^{\circ}$, and $A$ lies $29.27\ldots^{\circ}$ anticlockwise of $CB$.
$308^{\circ}-29.27\ldots^{\circ}\approx 279^{\circ}\text{T}$

1. **Select the rule that fits what is given**
Two sides and the included angle give $BC$ by the **cosine rule**.
$BC^{2}=85^{2}+64^{2}-2(85)(64)\cos 118^{\circ}$
$BC=\sqrt{11321-10880\cos 118^{\circ}}$
$=128.175\ldots$
$\approx 128.2$ m
2. **Apply a second rule to reach the required value**
A complete pair ($BC$ opposite $118^{\circ}$) is now known, so use the **sine rule** for $\angle ABC$, opposite $AC=64$.
$\dfrac{\sin\angle ABC}{64}=\dfrac{\sin 118^{\circ}}{128.175\ldots}$
$\angle ABC=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{64\sin 118^{\circ}}{128.175\ldots}\right)$
$\approx 26^{\circ}$

1. **Select the rule that fits what is given**
The area rule needs an angle. With three sides, find $\angle C$ (between $CA=150$ and $CB=190$, opposite $AB=210$) by the **cosine rule**.
$\cos C=\dfrac{150^{2}+190^{2}-210^{2}}{2(150)(190)}$
$\cos C=\dfrac{14500}{57000}$
$C=\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{14500}{57000}\right)=75.263\ldots^{\circ}$
2. **Apply a second rule to reach the required value**
$A=\dfrac{1}{2}(150)(190)\sin 75.263\ldots^{\circ}$
$\approx 13\,781\text{ m}^{2}$
